The role is accountable for translating business intent into a scalable technical landscape, owning solution direction from discovery and architecture definition through delivery governance and production stability. The architect is expected to actively shape scope and commercial outcomes, driving decisions on what should be configured out-of-the-box (OOB) versus custom-built, while minimizing customization wherever the platform’s native capability can meet the need. Key Responsibilities Define and own end-to-end enterprise architecture across OMS core, extension microservices, integration layers, and downstream systems. Translate business and functional requirements into technical solutions, ensuring alignment with business outcomes. Architect custom microservices as OMS extension points using cloud-native and event-driven patterns. Own non-functional requirements, including scalability, resiliency, security, latency, and cost. Collaborate with business, technology, and ISV teams to define scope, estimates, timelines, milestones, and phased delivery plans. Provide cost inputs and trade-off analysis (build vs. configure, in-house vs. ISV-delivered). Evaluate requirements against OMS OOB capabilities before recommending customization. Document OOB versus custom decisions and rationale. Define architectural standards, coding guidelines, integration patterns, and governance processes. Establish architecture review checkpoints and maintain architecture documentation. Lead solution workshops, architecture reviews, and trade-off discussions with business and technical stakeholders. Represent architecture decisions in client governance forums. Domain & Technical Expertise Strong B2B OMS domain knowledge, including order lifecycle, inventory/allocation, fulfillment orchestration, and returns. Knowledge of OMS integrations with Payment Gateways, PLM, Loyalty Platforms, Recommendation Engines, WMS, and Promotion Frameworks. Expertise in Java/J2EE, microservices, event-driven architecture, RESTful services, and integration patterns. Strong understanding of cloud architecture, preferably AWS, including Lambda, API Gateway, CloudWatch, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Kinesis, Secrets Manager, and S3. Experience evaluating serverless, containerized, and server-based architectures. Engineering, Governance & Support Define and enforce Agile delivery practices, architecture governance, and CI/CD standards. Review delivery execution and ensure alignment with architectural standards. Define observability strategies using New Relic, Datadog, Grafana, and Splunk. Guide L3 support processes and work with L1/L2 teams to resolve systemic issues. Proactively identify recurring issue patterns and drive automation opportunities. Troubleshoot and resolve cross-functional production issues requiring architectural judgment. Required Qualifications 12+ years of technology experience, including architecture, technical leadership, or solutioning ownership. Prior OMS implementation experience is mandatory; Burgeon OMS experience preferred. Experience building custom microservices as extension points to commercial OMS platforms. Must be locally based in China. Business proficiency in Mandarin and English (spoken and written). Proven experience defining scope, estimates, timelines, and phased delivery plans in client-facing engagements. Ability to operate effectively at both business and technical levels. Flexibility to overlap with IST and PST hours for client meetings and governance activities.

review_candidates.title: Marketing Associate
review_candidates.description: Who is Understory? Understory is a vertical-focused software platform built for experience businesses – from kayaking tours to cooking classes. Our operating system helps creators manage operations, grow bookings, accept payments, and run their business with clarity and less stress. We move fast, iterate quickly, and expect everyone to bring proactive solutions every day. You'll learn faster here than almost anywhere else because the challenges are real and the pace is high. This isn't about clocking in and out – the right candidate will get a lot of trust and ownership, and it's all about building something that matters to creators around the world. We recently raised a €12M Series A and are scaling fast. With customers in 10+ countries and a growing presence internationally, our focus is global, our ambition is high, and our team is fully committed to being the go-to platform for experience creators worldwide. In keeping with this momentum, we're growing Marketing Operations in Aarhus, the team that runs the marketing products our customers use to grow their business. The team Marketing Operations is part of our Product organization and runs our marketing products for customers: Meta Ads, Google Ads, websites and reviews, with more on the way. Some are fully automated, some run on their own with people overseeing them, and some have a person in the loop at key steps. The team is AI-native: agents and in-house tools do much of the production and optimization, and people steer, check and improve the work. Next, we're becoming AI-led: the tools take on more of the production, and people spend more of their time on judgment and quality. You'll learn that way of working from day one. The team is three people today and growing. About the role This is an entry-level role for someone early in their career, for example fresh out of university or just getting started. You don't need prior marketing experience. You need to be sharp, structured and ready to learn fast. As a Marketing Associate you help deliver our marketing products to customers, reliably and to a high standard. You work with templates, SOPs and a shared task queue, and our AI tools and agents do much of the production. You steer, check and finish the work so campaigns go live on time and with consistent quality. We train you in the tools and workflows, and you help improve them as part of a team that relies on each other. What you'll do Create and quality-check ad assets using our templates, AI tools and standards Pick up customer requests from the team's shared queue and see them through to launch Schedule approved campaigns to go live on the agreed date and handle customer revisions quickly Support weekly performance reviews for customers using our standard method Work closely with your team and Customer Success Flag what slows you down or causes rework, so the team and Product can fix it What success looks like In your first three months, you will: Learn our templates, tools and workflows inside out Deliver ads with minimal rework Handle customer requests reliably and on time Keep your task status accurate so the team can always trust it Take customer requests from brief to live campaign independently by month three We think you'll thrive if… You're low ego, high agency and kind: you take initiative, make your colleagues' work easier, take feedback well and ask for help when you need it You like structure: clear processes and deadlines help you do your best work You care about your work: you finish what you start, and when something is at risk of slipping, you spot it early, say so and help fix it You notice details others miss and take pride in work you'd be happy to put your name on You're curious and eager to learn new tools, including AI tools You have full professional proficiency in English It's a plus if you… Have experience with Canva or Figma Are familiar with HubSpot or other marketing tools Have a basic understanding of paid advertising Have completed or are pursuing studies in a relevant field Have had professional or academic exposure to marketing or operations Speak Spanish or Italian with full professional proficiency If you recognize yourself in most of this, but not all, we would still like to hear from you. We care most about how you think and how you work with people. What it's like to work at Understory We are product-minded, mission-driven and serious about quality, in the product, the strategy and how we work together. We think long-term and keep evolving, as individuals and as a company. There is room to grow here, and the chance to help shape something category-defining. Practical information Hours: Full-time Duration: Ongoing employment Location: Aarhus (80% in-office) Team: Marketing Operations (Product) Reports to: Christian Berndt, VP of Product Preferred start date: 2026, flexible We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis and will hire as soon as we find the right person, so don't wait to apply.

review_candidates.title: Manager, Mental Health - Canada
review_candidates.description: Men are dying too young - and it doesn’t have to be that way. Around the world, men are facing a health crisis: prostate cancer, testicular cancer, poor mental health and suicide. At Movember we’re on a mission to change the face of men’s health by making it easier for men to talk, act and live longer healthier lives. Every project, every campaign, every idea adds up to real change. You’ll be part of a mustache-powered crew who believe making an impact and having fun should go hand in hand. Your mission is calling. DO GOOD. Work for Movember. Your Mo-Mission (should You Choose To Accept It) Most program roles come with one clear remit. This one comes with two, and the second is genuinely rare. As Manager, Mental Health, Canada, you’ll lead the in-market delivery of Movember’s mental health programs across Canada, to time, quality, and budget. But alongside that, you’ll hold global accountability as Global Lead for the Global Youth Advisory Network, driving its multi-year growth and long-term sustainability across all of Movember’s markets. Canadian delivery is the baseline. The global youth advisory lead is what sets this role apart. On the Canadian side, you’ll operationalise approved implementation plans across the full portfolio: sport-health, esports and gaming, community, research, online, grant delivery, and youth advisory. You’ll build strategic and delivery partnerships, hold accountability for program outcomes against agreed KPIs, manage in-market budgets including forecasting, variance reporting, and reallocation recommendations, and lead, mentor, and coach a growing team. On the global youth advisory side, you’ll be Movember’s external lead, representing the organisation with funders, government, partners, and sector bodies. You’ll own governance, terms of reference, and the recruitment, remuneration, and duty of care of young advisors and alumni across markets. You’ll manage the Canadian youth advisory directly, partnering with a delivery organisation to recruit and facilitate Mo-YAC Canada, run co-design activity, and feed market insight into the global function. And you’ll embed youth lived experience into portfolio design and investment decisions across all markets, influencing colleagues who sit outside your reporting line. This is a role for someone who can hold both of these responsibilities simultaneously, without either becoming a secondary priority. You’ll need the credibility to represent Movember, the operational rigour to run complex multi-program implementation, and a genuine commitment to the belief that young men deserve better mental health support than they currently get. This is a two-year fixed term contract due to an internal secondment/ promotion. No Moustache Required - But The Following Are At least four years of experience in program or portfolio implementation, including a sustained period of accountability for a defined strategy, function, or market. A tertiary qualification in a relevant field such as public health, health promotion, social sciences, or program and project management, or equivalent occupational experience. Demonstrated ability to lead and influence with minimal direct line authority across geographies and functions, and to represent Movember externally at a senior level with funders, government, and advisory bodies. Sound understanding of men’s and young men’s mental health and the broader health sector. Demonstrated budget accountability and investment recommendation experience, including contract management, negotiation, and strong commercial and policy acumen. Safeguarding practice and demonstrated experience working with young people in an advisory or co-design capacity, which is essential for the Youth Advisory accountability. Not Mission Critical - But For Extra Bonus Points Understanding and experience of grant management, and of organised sport, esports, and online community settings. Experience in the mental health, organised sport, education and training, or not-for-profit sectors. Bilingual in English and French, which is an asset for the Canadian market. Good Cause Working for Movember, you’ll help turn ideas (and moustaches) into millions for men’s health. Every bit we raise changes the face of men’s health by funding research, improving treatments, and supporting programs that help save lives. We’re even shaping government policies on men’s health worldwide. By meeting directly with lawmakers, and helping them understand how more investment on men’s health benefits not just men, but all the communities they serve. Good Vibes We love weekends. That’s why our Fridays finish early for nine months of the year. But we also love our office vibe. Because here, it always feels like something big is about to happen. Be it an office-wide surprise birthday party (with cake!) or an open invite for all to hit the pub. Come the hairy season, the energy cranks up. We’re talking celebrity visits. Live stunts on-site for TV and radio. And when we hit a fundraising milestone, the office gong might even go off. But, for those who prefer calm, no probs: hybrid working means you work where you feel best. Good Crew Spoiler alert: we’re a no-ego, all-impact crew. That means everyone gets a say, from new starters to those leading the charge. Collaboration over hierarchies, curiosity over rigid process. And it’s true across all our offices worldwide. We work as one, sharing expertise and celebrating wins. All in the name of making the biggest impact across the globe. United, we Mo. Boy, do we know the feeling of being judged. (Over how we look, and other things that shouldn’t matter.) Being different is how we started. And it’s also helped us raise $1 billion for men’s health. So, we know the power of diverse experiences, skills and perspectives. Movember is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive community and workplace - a place where we can all be ourselves, and each have the equal opportunity to succeed and be recognised for our unique contribution. We value the experiences, skills and perspectives of all individuals and actively encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds. We make recruitment decisions based on applicants’ skills, experience, and knowledge, ensuring all applicants are treated fairly. Reasonable accommodations are also available on request for differently abled candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. A quick note on AI We use our AI mate Joel to help with the first stage of screening. It lets more great candidates move past the application stage and into the process faster. Don’t worry though, real humans make all the final decisions. And if you’d rather skip Joel and chat with a recruiter instead, you’ll always have that option. Do you want to DO GOOD? If so, we’d love to hear from you. Movember is the global leader in men’s health. Our focus is on mental health, suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer. Since beginning over drinks at a bar in 2003 in Melbourne, we’ve expanded internationally, raised over $1 billion for men’s health and funded more than 1,320 men’s health related projects globally.

review_candidates.title: Ingénieur études système d'intégration F/H
review_candidates.description: Au Sein De La Direction Engineering, Vous Intégrerez Le Département "Etudes Systèmes Aéroportés". La Mise En Oeuvre D'un Missile Aéroporté Se Fait Au Travers D'une Fonction Embarquée Dans L'aéronef Appelée Conduite De Tir. Cette Fonction Est En Interface Avec Le Pilote, L'avion Et Le Missile Et Est Supportée Par Des Dispositifs Matériels Et Logiciels. Elle a Pour Objectif De Faire En Sorte Que Les Deux Systèmes Complexes Que Sont La Plateforme D'une Part Et Le Missile D'autre Part Fonctionnent Ensemble De Façon Cohérente Et Optimale. Les Algorithmes Concernés Reposent Classiquement Sur Des Modèles Missile Également Intégrés Aux Moyens De Simulation Utilisés Pour L'Entraînement Des Pilotes Afin D'appréhender La Performance De Nos Produits Et De Diverses Menaces. Dans Le Cadre De L'intégration D'un Missile Sur Une Plateforme Aéroportée, La Mission Permanente Du Poste Consiste à Participer Aux Études De Définition Fonctionnelle Des Moyens Nécessaires à La Mise En Oeuvre Du Missile (conduite De Tir), Des Moyens Sol Associés (entraînement) Et à Déterminer La Performance Du Système Global Missile + Plateforme (études Système De Performance Installée). Vos Missions Seront Les Suivantes Assurer la conception fonctionnelle d'une ou plusieurs conduites de tir, - Réaliser des études de concept de mise en oeuvre notamment des réflexions sur les IHM, - Mener des travaux sur les algorithmes embarqués en lien avec cette équipe, - Étudier les moyens d'entrainement ou de simulation à travers l'utilisation de ces algorithmes, - Définir une partie de l'architecture système et mener les études de performances embarquées, - Optimiser l'interfaçage entre le pilote, l'avion et le missile et en assurer la cohérence, - Soutenir l'équipe dans la préparation et à l'analyse de tirs d'essais ou tirs client. Notre rémunération comporte un salaire fixe et des éléments additionnels individuels (une part variable pour nos salariés cadres et une prime d'ancienneté ainsi qu'une prime annuelle pour nos salariés non-cadres) ou collectifs dépendant de la performance et des résultats de l'entreprise (participation, intéressement). De nombreux services/avantages sont également proposés : restaurant d'entreprise, épargne salariale (PEG, PERCOL), protection sociale (mutuelle et prévoyance), comité social et économique, infirmerie et service de santé au travail interne... Un poste stratégique qui offre une vision d'ensemble des activités et vous permettra d'intervenir, en fonction des besoins et projets, sur trois domaines clés : la conduite de tir, les systèmes d'entraînement et les études systèmes. - Une grande diversité de missions, allant de la conception aux essais terrain - Une forte autonomie dans vos projets, tout en évoluant au sein d'une équipe dynamique - Des interactions multiples avec des experts internes et des partenaires externes , Diplômé d'une école d'ingénieur généraliste ou équivalent, vous justifiez d'une connaissance en aéronautique. Vous possédez des compétences générales dans les disciplines de l'aéronautique (mécanique du vol, aérodynamique, ...). Une connaissance de MATLAB est un atout. Compte tenu de l'environnement international de MBDA, un bon niveau d'anglais est nécessaire. Capacités de raissonnement, bon sens, curiosité sont impératifs. Des déplacements occasionnels sont à prévoir chez les partenaires industriels et interlocuteurs étatiques en région parisienne ou les utilisateurs sur base militaire en France, généralement sur la journée. Etablissement soumis à enquête administrative conformément aux dispositions des articles R.2311-1 et suivants du Code de la défense et de l'IGI n°1300 du 9 août 2021. 006, MBDA est l’un des leaders mondiaux dans la conception, le développement et la commercialisation de missiles et systèmes d'armements complexes. Seul Groupe capable de répondre à toute la gamme des besoins opérationnels présents et futurs des trois forces armées (Terre, Marine, Air et Espace), notre entreprise regroupe plus de 20 000 collaborateurs (dont 8 000 en France) animés par la passion de la haute technologie et l’esprit de défense . Avec un chiffre d’affaires annuel de 5,8Md€ en 2024, notre société est une filiale commune de Airbus (37,5 %), BAE Systems (37,5 %), et Leonardo (25 %). Cette année en France, MBDA ouvre plus de 1 500 postes dont 1 000 CDI, 500 alternances, CDD et offres de stages !
